title: The Falling House (flashback-frame, four threads)
source: Hand-authored, Set B (flashback/frame) x multi-thread, expanded

threads.label: Elena, the night of the fire (told via flashback framing)
Marta, Elena's sister, recalling that same night (a nested flashback within the flashback)

events.text: The inspector opens the arson case file on Monday morning.
Three nights before the fire, Elena had already hidden a spare key under the mat.
On Tuesday, he re-interviews the landlord about the building's history.
The next night, Elena let herself in with the hidden key just as the neighbor's dog stopped barking.
Elena's flashlight beam vanished from the window the instant the smoke alarm began to blare.
That same night, Mrs. Kade had been logging every noise from the house since sundown, and her log entry ends the moment the alarm sounds.
By Wednesday, he learns the landlord filed an insurance claim the same week as the fire.
Mrs. Kade's full week of notes, spanning Monday through Sunday, entirely contains the single night of the fire.
He arrests Elena on Thursday, one day after learning of the claim.
That same Monday afternoon, Voss walks the scorched ground floor of the house himself.
By Tuesday evening, he has the fire marshal's forensic report open on his desk.
Wednesday afternoon, Voss requests a warrant for the landlord's financial records.
Thursday afternoon, Voss books Elena into holding after the arrest.
By Friday, Voss closes the file, satisfied the timeline finally holds together.

events.time_expr: earlier that same night, before letting herself in
events.text: Earlier that same night, before letting herself in, Elena had watched the house from across the street.

events.time_expr: just inside the door, moments after entering
events.text: Just inside the door, Elena's flashlight beam swept the dark hallway.
Minutes later, in the study, Elena rifled through a drawer of the landlord's old papers.

events.time_expr: as she straightened from the drawer
events.text: As Elena straightened from the drawer, a curl of smoke reached the ceiling behind her.

events.time_expr: in the seconds after the alarm
events.text: In the seconds after the alarm, Elena bolted for the back door.

events.time_expr: by the time she reached the street
events.text: By the time she reached the street, sirens were already rising in the distance.
At nine that night, Marta had been pacing by the phone, waiting for Elena to call.

events.time_expr: twenty past nine until just after ten
events.text: By twenty past nine, Marta had driven to the street and sat idling in her car a block away.

events.time_expr: shortly before ten, from the car
events.text: From the car, Marta watched Elena slip through the gate just as the porch light flickered.
Minutes later, Marta checked her phone again for a message that never came.
The instant the alarm's wail reached the car, Marta's stomach dropped.
Moments after, Marta saw the first flashing lights before Elena reappeared at the corner.
She pulled the car around to the back street to meet her.

events.time_expr: in the drive away from the scene
events.text: She drove Elena away from the scene, taking the long way past the river.
In the weeks that followed, Marta rehearsed the story so often in her head that she began to believe her own version of it.
That Monday, Mrs. Kade's log records a quiet evening with no visitors.
On Tuesday, she notes the landlord's car idling outside twice.

events.time_expr: within minutes of the alarm, that same night
events.text: Within minutes of the alarm, she logs the fire trucks arriving on the street.
By Thursday, her log notes reporters gathering outside the gate.
Friday's entry records the insurance adjuster's visit to the wreckage.
On Saturday, she notes the house finally sealed behind police tape.
Her final entry, on Sunday, notes the street was quiet again.
